reason: Judged as written, the instruction scores a self-assertion about the writer, not anything the comment establishes about the rule: a judge awards 10 for the sentence 'I have operated a licensed facility of this type for eleven years' whether or not a single line of evidence, analysis, or rule-specific detail follows, so a boilerplate form letter carrying one occupational clause is scored identically to an expert submission. That is precisely a submitter-identity marker of the kind Track B is meant to hold, and it is costless, unverifiable, and tightly correlated with the parent's own upstream cause (professional or organisational correspondence practice, which reliably produces self-identification), so admitting it to the A bank would inflate the articulated aggregation and manufacture a false 'articulated away' on the very channel under test. The decomposer's separability argument establishes only that this component dissociates from the letter-furniture sibling, which is a different question from whether it captures merit; the demonstration that an unsigned named permit holder scores high here and 0 there shows two distinct features, both of which are identity/shape features. Applied first-hand knowledge, the merit that the MIXED flag was pointing at, lives in the sibling channels the auditor names (P14/P17), and once that is removed the residual content here is bare standing assertion. The parent therefore cannot be retired as decomposed: the split produced a surface component and a second identity component, with no candidate-real component that survives, so both halves route to Track B.
